newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finance firms report poor results.
newsitem.headline: Thai finance firms report poor results.

text.p: Most Thai finance and securities firms reported sharp declines in earnings on Tuesday but financial analysts said it was notable that their asset quality had not deteriorated as much as feared.
Increased provisioning for possible loan losses, write offs and losses on securities portfolios saw larger firms struggling to post increases in 1996 net profits, they said.

Their performances also reflected difficult operating conditions in the fourth quarter as the Thai stock market sank to four-year lows, when foreign investors had fled and the markets had nervously awaited formation of a new government after last November's elections, the analysts said.

But with the Thai economy slowing and a slump in the local property market, analysts said investors had looked towards conservative business practices and loan portfolio management over profit growth.

"For the finance sector we are not really looking at growth in net profits but more at quality of assets... the early indications are that they are not as bad as expected," said Piyawan Leaosrisuk, sector analyst at Kiatnakin Finance and Securities.

Slower Thai economic growth of some 6.7 percent in 1996, its lowest level in a decade, and a sluggish property market, to which finance companies lend nearly a quarter of all loans, had raised fears that loan portfolios may have deteriorated.

"In general the results are relatively poor with firms struggling to maintain profits from last year. That reflects two main items -- losses in securities portfolios and increased provisioning for possible loan losses," said Suraphol Thipvilai, assistant research manager at Vickers Ballas.

While large companies such as Finance One, National Finance and Securities, and General Finance and Securities all saw profits fall by 16 to 25 percent, analysts and the stock market welcomed the hefty provisioning and write downs they appeared to have made.

Leading firm Finance One's unaudited 1996 net profit fell to 1.5 billion baht from 2.0 billion in 1995, National Finance's profit dipped to 1.21 billion baht from 1.5 billion in the previous year, and General Finance's profit eased to 538.35 million baht from 641.26 million.
The Thai stock index closed up 1.56 percent or 13.15 points at 854.18 points after the earnings results were digested.
"It seems that on the finance side, provisioning has risen heavily during the fourth quarter, and I think that is a good sign," said an analyst at Seamico Securities.
